content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I have a system using a [product_name] PLC and multiple drives. When it runs, the relay outputs repeatedly switch off and on. What could be the solution for this issue?

• How have you confirmed that the PLC program itself isn't faulty? (Is this a [company_name] [product_name] programmable relay or a different model?) • What led you to suspect that electrical noise is causing the problem? • What is the actual current drawn through the output connected to the drive? • Have you checked the drive's manual for recommendations about filtering at the power input? • Did you test for short circuits between the PLC and the drive? • Have you verified that the PLC and the drives are sharing the same ground reference and are properly earthed? You could try connecting the PLC output to the coil of an external relay, then use its Normally Open contact to operate the drive. Observe how both the relay and drive respond during this test.

analysis.insight_summary: The user is experiencing relay outputs repeatedly switching on and off when the system, consisting of a [product_name] PLC and several drives, is in operation. Community responses cover potential causes like programming errors, electrical interference, wiring issues, and grounding, highlighting the difficulty in pinpointing the problem within a complex setup. There is ongoing uncertainty about whether the fault is inherent to the product or arises from system integration and configuration, reflecting the challenges of troubleshooting in multifaceted environments.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects stable, dependable relay outputs from the PLC even when linked to drives, without any unwanted cycling. They seek a simple solution to eliminate this interference and achieve consistent operation.
